questions.text: Tell me about a customer you saved from churning. What was your read on the real reason they were leaving?
questions.rationale: Churn saves reveal diagnostic skill; the stated reason is rarely the real one.

questions.text: Describe a customer you could not save. Looking back, when was the save actually lost?
questions.rationale: Tests whether the candidate understands churn as a lagging indicator of earlier failures.

questions.text: How do you run a quarterly business review that executives actually attend? What is on your agenda?
questions.rationale: QBR quality separates strategic CSMs from check-in schedulers.

questions.text: Walk me through your onboarding playbook for a new account. Where do accounts most often stall?
questions.rationale: Onboarding is the highest-leverage CS motion; the stall answer shows real experience.

questions.text: Tell me about a time a customer demanded a feature you knew was not coming. How did you handle it?
questions.rationale: Tests honest expectation-setting versus placation that erodes trust later.

questions.text: How do you identify expansion opportunities without turning every call into a sales pitch?
questions.rationale: The expansion-versus-trust balance is the modern CS role's core tension.

questions.text: Describe a time you escalated on behalf of a customer internally and got pushback. What did you do?
questions.rationale: Screens for customer advocacy with organizational skill rather than volume.

questions.text: What drew you to customer success rather than sales or support?
questions.rationale: Tests understanding of the role's actual shape and whether it matches their energy.

questions.text: Tell me about your most demanding customer ever. How did you keep the relationship healthy?
questions.rationale: Boundary-setting with difficult accounts, screened through a real story.

questions.text: How do you prioritize a book of forty accounts? Which ones get your proactive time?
questions.rationale: Portfolio thinking separates proactive CSMs from inbox responders.

questions.text: Describe a health score or early warning system you have used. When did it fail you?
questions.rationale: The failure half screens for sophistication about metrics versus dashboard faith.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you delivered bad news to a customer: an outage, a deprecation, a price change. How did you frame it?
questions.rationale: Bad-news delivery is a craft; framing choices reveal maturity.

questions.text: What does a great relationship between CS and product look like? Describe the best or worst version you have lived.
questions.rationale: CS is the voice of the customer only if the feedback loop works; tests loop-building instinct.

questions.text: How do you turn a frustrated power user into a champion? Give a real example.
questions.rationale: Champion cultivation is a repeatable skill; a specific story proves it.

questions.text: Describe your note-taking and handoff discipline. If you left tomorrow, what would your successor find?
questions.rationale: Documentation hygiene protects customers from personnel changes; a fair junior-level bar.

questions.text: Tell me about a renewal negotiation where the customer had real leverage. How did it resolve?
questions.rationale: Commercial spine in the renewal moment, where CS work becomes measurable.

questions.text: What is your approach in the first call with an account that has been ignored for six months?
questions.rationale: Rebuilding trust from neglect is a common inherited situation; tests candid reset instincts.

questions.text: How do you measure your own success in this role beyond retention numbers?
questions.rationale: Reveals the candidate's internal scorecard and its alignment with customer outcomes.

questions.text: Describe a time you noticed a pattern across several accounts and pushed a systemic fix.
questions.rationale: Pattern-level advocacy separates future CS leaders from individually excellent CSMs.

questions.text: Tell me about a colleague relationship that made your CS work better. What did you build together?
questions.rationale: CS quality depends on internal relationships; screens for deliberate relationship-building.

questions.text: How do you handle a customer who treats your team disrespectfully but pays a lot?
questions.rationale: Values-under-revenue-pressure question; the answer reveals what the candidate will tolerate.

questions.text: Walk me through how you learn a customer's business well enough to advise them. How long until you are credible?
questions.rationale: Consultative credibility requires method; tests whether one exists.

questions.text: Describe your experience with support ticket escalations. Where does CS end and support begin for you?
questions.rationale: Role boundary clarity prevents the CSM-as-supersupport failure mode.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you said no to a customer request and kept the relationship strong.
questions.rationale: No-with-relationship-intact is the daily CS skill most candidates cannot evidence.

questions.text: As a CS lead, how do you set coverage models and books? What tradeoff did you get wrong the first time?
questions.rationale: Operating model experience with an honest-mistake probe built in.

questions.text: What keeps you energized in a role where the wins are quiet and the losses are loud?
questions.rationale: Sustainable motivation in a low-glory role predicts tenure.

questions.text: Describe how you have used product usage data in a customer conversation. What did you see and what did you do?
questions.rationale: Data-informed conversations are table stakes; tests actual fluency, not tool listing.

questions.text: Tell me about onboarding yourself into a product you had never used. How fast were you demo-ready?
questions.rationale: Self-serve learning speed matters in fast-changing products.

questions.text: How would you rebuild trust after our own product caused a customer's worst week of the quarter?
questions.rationale: Accountability without deflection, tested in the hardest realistic scenario.

questions.text: What team norms would you bring with you from your last CS team, and which would you leave behind?
questions.rationale: Culture-add framing that also surfaces what the candidate disliked living under.
